messages:
ara: Heads-up: prod-eu-north1 is showing a weird packing hole. Lots of tiny inference pods pending while several nodes show fractional free GPUs. This started ~25m ago. :thinking_face:
ben: can you share the grafana panels? is it pending_gpus or pending_pods?
ara: panels: cluster/allocations -> gpu_pending_count + node/gpu_free_fraction. Numbers: pending=84, fractional_free_nodes=6, avg_free_fraction=0.5 GPUs on each.
chloe: did the nvlink topology label rollout finish? last night we applied `nvlink-group` labels so training jobs prefer NVLink peers. Could be blocking packing.
diego: scheduler logs show the affinity plugin rejecting co-locate attempts for tiny pods because node has `nvlink-group=1` and pods with `workloadClass=training` are being prioritized incorrectly. The matching code treats nvlink-group as a hard affinity if any training workload exists on the node.
ara: pasted `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending` (truncated):
```
# kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending
mini-infer-9          Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector
rerank-job-44         Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
```
ben: autoscaler shows a scale attempt at 1800055600 but cloud returned `QuotaExceeded: GPUs requested 10, quota 6`. Also spot-requests failing in region.
infra-bot: ALERT: [gpu-pending-pods] cluster-prod-eu-north1 threshold breached (count=84) at 1800055590
chloe: immediate mitigation options: 1) add tolerations to tiny inference deployments for `nvlink-group` taint (if taint present) 2) flip scheduler flag to allow per-class fractional coalescing (tiny only) 3) temporarily relax `nvlink-group` matching to soft preference.
diego: note: dropping nvlink affinity to soft may cause multi-job NVLink-unfriendly packing for large training jobs, affecting inter-GPU bandwidth. Risk: training job slowdown.
ara: I patched a non-critical tiny deployment to annotate `scheduler.alpha/coalesce=allow-tiny` and it landed on nodes with fractional free GPUs. Example patch I used:
```
kubectl patch deploy mini-infer -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/metadata/annotations/scheduler.alpha~1coalesce","value":"allow-tiny"}]'
```
ben: after applying to 10% of tiny pods, pending dropped from 84 -> 26 in ~7m and warmpool util rose from 22% -> 54%. But we saw a small cross-AZ egress blip for a few pods (~3% traffic spike).
chloe: opened ticket CLOUD-9401 for quota bump and to check spot capacity. Also INFRA-2072 to track scheduler nvlink affinity bug + rollout gating.
infra-bot: Action: scaled provisioner to 3 replicas by chloe at 1800055622. JobID=scale-1800055622
diego: long-term fixes (putting on infra-scheduler backlog): - make nvlink-group a soft preference for tiny/background workloads - implement per-workload coalesce whitelist - add rollout gate that blocks label/taint agent if pending_gpus > 15 for 15m - add simulated packing check in CI to catch this class of regressions.
ben: for now we should also add an emergency playbook: 1) annotate tiny deployments with coalesce allow 2) if quota allows, spin a small spot pool with tiny-pool label in neighboring region 3) revert node-label agent change if rollback threshold met. I'll draft the runbook steps.
ara: created INFRA-2072 with runbook stub and assigned owners @diego (scheduler), @chloe (cloud-ops), @ben (runbook). Leaving alerts on.
ops-bot: Incident INFRA-2072 created by chloe at 1800055640.
infra-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: pending_gpus dropped to 18 at 1800055668.
chloe: follow-up: let's add a canary for the node-label agent: 1) 5% node rollout, 2) measure pending_gpus delta over 20m, 3) abort if delta > 10. I'll open a PR for the agent.
diego: agreed. Also let's add a preflight quota check to the rollout pipeline to avoid hitting hard quota caps.
ara: thanks everyone — I'll post the INFRA-2072 summary in #eng-infra once it's filled out. :thumbsup:
